name: Oort Cloud
story: A hypothetical spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the entire solar system — extending from roughly 2,000 to 100,000 AU. Never directly observed, only inferred: the long-period comets we see have orbits so wide they must come from out here. Estimated population: trillions of bodies. The Oort cloud represents the solar system's birth-cloud leftovers, dynamically stable for billions of years at this distance from the Sun. Passing stars can perturb individual objects inward, becoming the comets we observe.
comparison: Half a light-year out. The Sun's gravitational reach extends roughly to the inner Oort cloud edge — beyond that, the galaxy's tides start to dominate. The Voyagers will take 30,000 years just to reach the inner boundary.
